newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia central bank cuts discount rates - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia central bank cuts discount rates - dealers.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, cut its key discount rate for short-term securities (SBPUs) by 50 basis points on Thursday, dealers said.
"The central bank has cut discount rates by 50 basis points for all maturities on Thursday," one state bank dealer said.
The dealer said one-week money fell to 15.25 percent, two to 15.50 percent, one-, three-, six- and 12-month to 16.0 percent.
This was confirmed by the central bank.
SBPUs are papers purchased by the central bank to inject liquidity into the banking system.

Dealers said the rate for one-week central bank certificates (SBIs) was set at 11.50 percent on Thursday, two-week at 12.0 percent, one-month at 12.50 percent, three-month at 13.50 percent, six-month at 13.75 percent and 12-month at 14.00 percent.
SBIs are securities issued by the central bank to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system.
Dealers said the SBPU cut had been anticipated following declines of SBI rates by 50 basis points since early November.
